exercises.instruction: Match the words with a word from the box to give eight different forms or documents.
What are these forms and documents? (Many of them are from 83.1.)
items: 1 You fill this in when you are writing off for a job.
2 You may have to fill this in (often on a plane) when you enter another country.
3 This is put in your passport and gives you permission to enter, pass through or leave another country.
4 This card has your name on it and a photo to show who you are.
5 You often fill in one of these before you start a course, e.g. if you study English at a language school.
6 This card states that you are a member of a particular club or organisation.

exercises.instruction: Fill the gaps with the best word in these sentences.
items: 1 A: I've got a ten-year passport but it .................................. in two months' time.
B: But you're planning to go to Venezuela in October, aren't you?
A: Yes, I am, so I'd better .......................... it quickly, otherwise I'll be in trouble.
2 A: When I've completed this form, do I have to .................................. it at the bottom?
B: Yes, please. Put your .................................. just there, and next to it put today's date.

exercises.instruction: An official is questioning someone who has just arrived in this country. Complete the questions.
items: B: I got here two days ago.
B: In ten days' time. My flight is on the 21st.

exercises.instruction: In written English, the questions in 83.4 are often expressed differently. Complete these expressions.
Find words on the right that have the same meaning as the verbs on the left.
items: 1 fill in    a stand in line
